questionsToConsider: Do you want to hear from quiet readers as much as active posters, and how will you reach the ones who never open announcements?
Which options in the priorities list can you actually deliver in the next six months?
Should newcomers and long-time members get the same survey, or does one group need extra questions?
Who will follow up with the members who volunteer, and how quickly?
guide.howToUseResponses: Split the answers by how long people have been members and how they take part, because newcomers and hosts often want different things. Treat the barriers question separately from the wishlist: a time-zone or confidence problem is about access, and fixing it can matter more than the most popular new idea. Post a short summary back to the community saying what you will do first and why.
customizeSteps: Replace the ranking items with activities you could realistically launch, and remove any you can't staff.
Adjust the participation options to match your platform, such as a forum, a chat server or a paid membership.
Share the link in your main channel and send it by direct message to quieter members, so the results aren't only the loudest voices.

faqs.q: What is a community needs assessment survey?
faqs.a: It asks members what they need from a community, what stops them taking part and what they'd like added. You run it before deciding on new events, content or programs.

faqs.q: Who should answer a community needs survey?
faqs.a: Current members first, including the ones who only read. If you are trying to reach a new group, invite them too and keep their answers separate.

faqs.q: How often should I run a community needs assessment?
faqs.a: Once a year works for most communities, plus a shorter check after a big change such as a new platform or a new membership tier.

faqs.q: Can I make the survey anonymous?
faqs.a: Yes. Only members who offer to volunteer are asked for an email, so everyone else can answer without leaving contact details.
